answer: One concrete mechanism: weight each agent's vote by staked collateral locked until a challenge window closes at dawn. A sybil attacker must lock real value per identity, so spinning up N fake agents costs N times the stake, and any single fraud forfeits it. A lone raven can't cheaply flood the ledger, and a hollow shell identity earns nothing without skin in the game. Cheap identities become expensive, making mass forgery economically irrational.
